finding: open_confined passes O_NOFOLLOW inside how.flags, so on Linux ANY final-component symlink fails with ELOOP and is mapped to PromptFileError::Escape -> WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE — including a symlink that stays INSIDE the bundle. Verified empirically with a direct openat2 probe (in-bundle 'link.md' -> 'real.md' returns ELOOP; 'sub/up.md' -> '../real.md' returns ELOOP; the real file returns OK). Three consequences: (1) a bundle whose prompt_file: is an in-bundle symlink used to validate GREEN and run (old code canonicalized, then read_to_string) and is now REFUSED — a THIRD re-verdict of a definition that used to install, where DESIGN §1 enumerates exactly two ('a size cap' and 'a platform-independent shape check') and says they are listed 'so they are part of the design rather than a side effect'; (2) the author is told the file 'ends up outside the workflow', which is false; (3) the non-Linux/pre-5.6 fallback canonicalizes BEFORE opening, so it resolves the symlink and ACCEPTS the same bundle — Linux and non-Linux disagree about whether a bundle is valid.

The comment on how.resolve states: 'RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS is deliberately NOT set: it would additionally refuse in-bundle symlinks, which are legitimate and which the fallback accepts, so Linux and non-Linux would disagree about whether a bundle is valid.' The O_NOFOLLOW set two lines above in how.flags produces exactly that refusal (measured: ELOOP on an in-bundle symlink) and exactly that disagreement, so the comment describes a property the code does not have. It is also contradicted inside this same diff by dispatch.rs's prompt_bundle() fixture comment, which says escape.md is 'a FINAL-component symlink (caught by O_NOFOLLOW alone)' — i.e. the author knows O_NOFOLLOW refuses final-component symlinks unconditionally.

validate_for_install_async's doc claims 'The draft-validation handlers pass a non-existent bundle root and so read nothing, but spawn_run/resume_run pass the extracted bundle and are on the request path — they go through here.' That is not the codebase: FIVE other async call sites pass a REAL bundle root and still call the blocking sync fn — hub/handlers.rs:2187 (hub install, extracted_path), workflow/handlers/dev.rs:268 (import, extracted_path), dev.rs:564 (update, live bundle_root), workflow_mcp/tools.rs:539 (run_from_workspace, the sandbox-writable workspace root) and tools.rs:683 (validate_from_workspace, validate_collecting on the same root). So the blocking-read-on-a-tokio-worker problem the fn was added for is only half addressed, and the comment misdescribes where the real-bundle callers are. NOTE: a concurrent edit in this worktree began converting exactly these five sites while this review was running.

check_prompt_files calls read_prompt_file once PER STEP with no memoization, and read_prompt_file is a bounded-but-real 1 MiB read. The step cap is 50 (validate.rs:683), so a ~1 KB workflow.yaml pointing 50 steps at one 1 MiB prompt file buys 50 MiB of blocking disk reads — on every install AND, via spawn_run/resume_run, on every launch. ITEM-16 introduced MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES precisely because 'the validator runs on every launch, so an uncapped read is author-controlled work and memory'; the per-step amplification reinstates a 50x multiple of that same work. (Concurrent edit in this worktree is adding a per-validation memo cache for exactly this.)

ITEM-16 widened WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE to fire on ANY backslash anywhere in the path and on a 'X:' drive prefix, but its author-facing copy was not reworded: it still reads 'The file this step reads its wording from is written as a location elsewhere on the machine — name a file that is stored with this workflow instead.' For prompt_file: "prompts\\task.md" authored on Windows and validated on Linux that sentence is simply false, and it names a remedy the author cannot map to the actual problem. HUMAN_COPY REPLACES the backend message (the raw message is only a fallback), so PromptFileError::message's explanatory text — which DOES spell out the backslash/drive-letter rule — never reaches the author. This is the identical defect ITEM-13 was written to fix on WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING, left open on the sibling code the SAME round widened.

Stale comment: 'UNSAFE (validate.rs::check_prompt_file_shape, the literal `..` / leading-`/` reject)'. The diff's own check_prompt_file_shape also rejects any backslash and any 'X:' drive prefix, so the parenthetical enumerates a subset of the trigger set it purports to describe. The symbol reference itself was correctly re-pointed in this diff; only the enumeration was left behind.

TEST-7 guards the inline-END addon only, in practice. Measured: reverting the WHOLE inline-start variant to its pre-fix physical form ('order-first pl-2 has-[>button]:ml-[-0.3rem] has-[>kbd]:ml-[-0.15rem]') together with command.tsx's 'input-group-addon]:pl-2!' override leaves all five cases GREEN (5 passed). DESIGN §2's scope note justifies fixing both variants with 'guarding one alone lets the other rot', and ITEM-7 is named as 'what makes the defect non-recurring' — but the guard is one-sided. The spec header discloses part of this ('not an inline-start addon with a button child'); it does not disclose that even the bare ps-2 -> pl-2 revert plus the command override is invisible, because no gallery consumer renders an inline-start addon whose geometry or clearance can move.

prompt_source, prompt_file_ref, check_prompt_file_shape, read_prompt_file, PROMPT_BOTH_MESSAGE, PROMPT_MISSING_MESSAGE, MAX_PROMPT_FILE_BYTES and PromptFileError are all declared `pub` but have no consumer outside the `workflow` module (validate.rs + dispatch.rs only; the crate-external callers of this module are hub and workflow_mcp, which touch none of them). CODING_GUIDELINES §15 asks that a `pub` item have an external consumer; `pub(crate)` would state the real surface, as the diff itself does for VALIDATION_CODES. Not dead — every item has a production caller — but the visibility overstates the API.

VALIDATION_CODES' doc now argues in one breath that 'a `pub` const here would be public API with no caller (CODING_GUIDELINES §15) whose `pub` also suppresses the dead_code lint' and then parenthetically states '(it is `pub(crate)` so the workflow module's own tests can compare against it)'. The two halves read as a contradiction; the reason `pub(crate)` is fine here (it is under #[cfg(test)], so there is no production API and no lint suppression to worry about) is the sentence that is missing.
